newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crude end higher amid scant trading.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crude end higher amid scant trading.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crude prices ended higher Thursday, amid scant talk and an absence of crude deals following the Christmas holiday.
Prices for Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude edged up with benchmark West Texas Intermediate (WTI) but discounts were unchanged. Most traders stayed out of the market in observance of the holiday.
The NYMEX crude futures market was open normal hours after an abbreviated Tuesday session.
The discount for ANS was $1.70 under WTI.
Flat diffs and higher WTI prices combined to lift up ANS five cents to $23.30/23.50 a barrel.
Kern River prices stayed at $18.65/18.75 a barrel after companies lifted postings late last week.
Discounts remained 10 cents below to even with postings, traders said.
Wilmington crude, produced offshore in Long Beach, Calif., also was flat at $20.15/20.25 a barrel.
